card.name: Te Kaimatoa
card.era: Traditional; widely practised in contemporary Kiribati
card.tagline: Kiribati 'dance of strength' testing the dancers' endurance
card.profile: Te Kaimatoa, literally the 'dance of strength,' is the most widely practised dance in contemporary Kiribati and is performed standing (Wikipedia: Dance in Kiribati). It tests the dancer's physical endurance to hold the arms outstretched for long periods as well as their emotional endurance; the music and rhythm are often highly emotive, and it is not uncommon to see dancers weep during performance. It can be performed by men, women and children, and is accompanied by a struck wooden box and vigorous choral singing.
card.insight: Te kaimatoa exemplifies the distinctive I-Kiribati dance aesthetic of outstretched, bird-like arms and sudden head movements inspired by the frigate bird that appears on the national flag (Wikipedia).
